SCCH 5 2. The brief facts of case is as under:
Deceased Muniraju, S/o.Annaiyappa was aged about 34 years, he was working as Mason and earning Rs.21,000/p.m., thereby maintaining his family.
3. That on 06.04.2022 at about 3.45 p.m. while standing beside the road to cross near Attibele border, opp. MCC Bar and Restaurant, NH7, HosurBengaluru Main Road, Attibele, Bengaluru, a bus bearing Reg.No.TN29N2710 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against said Muniraj, as a result he sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
4. Petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 is mother of the deceased Muniraj Annaiyappa, due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have lost their bread earner.

Out of the said accident,
crime No.103/2022 is registered against driver of the bus SCCH 5 before Attibele Police.

Respondent is owner and internal insurer of the bus bearing Reg.No.TN29N2710 is liable to pay compensation, so that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.36,00,000/.
5.

On service of notice, respondent has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioners, further taken contention that, place, date and time of the accident shall be strictly proved by the petitioners, they have to prove their relationship with deceased person, very accident is not occurred due to rash and negligent act of driver of the bus, claim made by petitioners is higher side, their petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Muniraj Annaiyappa,
S/o.Annaiyappa died in the motor vehicle accident hat occurred on 06.04.2022 at about 3.45 p.m. near Attibele Border, Opp. MCC Bar and Restaurant, NH7, Hosur Bengaluru Main Road, Attibele, Bengaluru at that time, Bus bearing Reg.No.TN29 N 2710 dashed against the deceased in a rash and negligently and deceased succumbed to death, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7.
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has deposed her evidence as PW1, marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, conductor in TNSTC is SCCH 5 examined as RW1, no documents got marked.
Accordingly his evidence is closed.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1: In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has deposed her evidence as PW1 by way of reiterating the facts narrated in their petition.

In support of their case they have furnished copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is SCCH 5 marked as Ex.P.5,
copy of inquest report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of P.M.Report is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of Charge Sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
10.

There is no crossexamination by way of denying the place, date and time of the accident by the said bus, further PW1 admits that, she is not eyewitness to the incident, further denied that,
deceased Muniraju was in drunken condition at the time of accident, further denied that, due to his own negligency this accident is caused.
Police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 supports the version of the petitioners and charge sheet is against the driver of the said bus.

11. On the other hand, there is evidence of conductor of the said bus as RW1, wherein he has denied the negligency of driver of the said bus, but admits that, there is no cross complaint against the SCCH 5 deceased and charge sheet is against driver of the said bus, further admits that, there is no document to show that, deceased was in drunken condition.

Looking to all these oral and documentary evidence, it reveals that, very accident is occurred only due to the negligency of the bus Smt. Roopa Chinnappa vs The Managing Director on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147530044/
3 driver, but not by the pedestrian.
12.

sentences.text: During argument counsel for respondent argued and relied on Ex.P.4/hand sketch prepared by Investigation Officer during investigation stating that, very accident is occurred in middle of the road, but on going through the hand sketch map it reveals that, deceased was on left edge of the road with view to cross the same, but bus driver came on very left edge of the road and dashed against the pedestrian, it goes to show that, defence taken by the counsel for the respondent during arguments is not sustainable.
Hence disbelieving SCCH 5 the version of the respondent and believing the version of the petitioners on the basis of available evidence, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was aged about 34 years as on the date of accident.

To prove the said facts, they have produced aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.11, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 19.07.1985 and the alleged accident is occurred on 06.04.2022, accordingly as on the date of the accident his age comes to 37 years, hence multiplier 15 is applicable with reference to the Sarla Verma case.

14. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as Mason and earning Rs.21,000/
p.m., but to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the SCCH 5 year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,500/ p.m.
15.

sentences.text: Further they have produced copy of aadhar card and voter ID Card marked as Ex.P.9 and Ex.P.10, it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased/Muniraj Annaiyappa, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

As per the case of the Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to 3 persons, then 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/3rd of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

16. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s.
SCCH 5 Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

In the case on hand, there is no self employment or fixed salary, but monthly annual income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.15,500/ hence,
which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 40% with reference to his age.
17. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.15,500/

(iv) Compensation after Rs.14,467/ x Rs.26,04,060/ multiplier of 15 is 12 x 15 applied 18.

Hence, petitioner No.1 being wife of the deceased is entitled for loss of consortium of Rs.40,000/, further petitioner No.2 being the mother of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/
towards filial consortium, further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/ and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.27,14,060/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
21.

In the case on hand, respondent being the insurercumowner of the bus bearing Reg.No.TN 29N 2710 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,14,060/ (Rupees Twenty Seven Lakhs Fourteen Thousand Sixty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

SCCH 5 The Petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
